steps: Join orders and customers on customer_id to get one row per order with the person's unique ID.
Group by customer_unique_id and count the number of orders per person, ignoring order status.
Calculate the repeat purchase rate as the proportion of customers with a count >= 2 out of the total number of customers.

data.text: Good, I can see the structure. Now let me run the SQL query to calculate the repeat purchase rate:

args.purpose: Calculate repeat purchase rate: share of customers with 2+ orders out of total customers
args.sql:
WITH customer_order_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    c.customer_unique_id,
    COUNT(o.order_id) as order_count
  FROM customers c
  JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
customer_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_count >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as repeat_customers,
    COUNT(*) as total_customers
  FROM customer_order_counts
)
SELECT 
  repeat_customers,
  total_customers,
  ROUND(100.0 * repeat_customers / total_customers, 2) as repeat_purchase_rate_pct
FROM customer_stats
